text: Main Stage, ground floor. Opening ceremony Friday 4pm to 6pm, Cal Band performance Friday 3:40pm, closing ceremony Sunday 2pm to 4pm, winners' photos Sunday 4pm to 5pm. Large sponsor talks happen here.
Hacking Floor A, ground floor, the main hall. Biggest hacking area with tables and power. Judging tables are assigned here on Sunday morning.
Hacking Floor B, ground floor. Second large hacking area with tables and power, usually quieter than Floor A.

Workshop Rooms, ground floor breakouts. All sponsor workshops run here on Saturday: Anthropic, Meta, Factory, Fetch.ai, Creao AI, Hyphenate, Bitdeer AI, Figma, Moss, SpaceXAI, Convex, Microsoft, Apify, Elastic, Visa, AfterQuery, Annapurna Labs, Bright Data, SpacetimeDB.
Mentor Tables, ground floor. Meet mentors in person for help with your project, or ask in the Slack channel #1-ask-mentors.
Food and Swag, ground floor. Meals, snacks and drinks are served here. The full menu and allergen list is linked from the hacker guide. Sponsor swag is handed out here too.
Robotics Space, ground floor. Hardware hacking area with room for robots and larger builds, next to the 3D printing station.

Mixers Area, ground floor. In-person team formation mixer after the opening ceremony on Friday. Entertainment events gather here: Clash Royale tournament, poker tournament, silent disco, haunted house making.
Sleeping Area, ground floor. Quiet overnight rest space. Staying overnight is optional and hotels are not reimbursed.
Theater, ground floor. Smaller talks, fireside chats such as Visa on AI and security in digital payments, and the Annapurna Labs technical domain talk.

Check-in and Info Desk, ground floor entrance. Check-in opens Friday 1:30pm. Bring a government-issued ID with date of birth and your digital Hacker Pass from the Hackathons @ Berkeley app. Lost and found, directors and general questions.
Relaxation Space, mezzanine. Quiet lounge for breaks away from the hacking floors.
Mezzanine Hacking, upstairs. Overflow hacking tables on the mezzanine, usually the quietest hacking spot.
Hardware Desk, mezzanine. Cal Hacks hardware rental booth, the MLH hardware lab and the 3D printing station. Borrow ESP32s, sensors, Arduinos and Raspberry Pis with your Hacker Pass.

Friday schedule: 1:30pm check-in begins at the Check-in desk. 3:40pm Cal Band performance on the Main Stage. 4pm to 6pm opening ceremony on the Main Stage. Team formation mixer in the Mixers Area after the ceremony. Friday night: Clash Royale tournament, midnight run, silent disco, poker tournament.
Saturday schedule: sponsor workshops all day in the Workshop Rooms. Sunrise hike Saturday morning. Haunted house making Saturday evening. Submit a draft on Devpost by Saturday night.

Sunday schedule: 9am project submission deadline on Devpost. 10:30am to 12:30pm judging at your assigned table on the hacking floor, the whole team must be present. 2pm to 4pm closing ceremony on the Main Stage. 4pm to 5pm winners' photos. Buses back to Montgomery BART from 3pm to 6:30pm from Palace Drive.

Hacker buses: free shuttle between Montgomery BART and the Palace of Fine Arts, every 15 minutes, 20 minute ride. Friday pickup at Sansome and Sutter from 1pm to 5:30pm. Sunday pickup at Palace Drive from 3pm to 6:30pm.

Parking and transport: no hacker parking at the venue. Rideshare should drop off a 5 to 10 minute walk away. Take BART into the city then Muni or Golden Gate Transit. The venue is at 3601 Lyon St, San Francisco, in the Marina District near Crissy Field and the Presidio.

Teams are 1 to 4 people. Find teammates in the Slack channel #1-team-formation, the Team Matching feature in the app, or the in-person mixer after the opening ceremony. Add teammates on Devpost when submitting.

Judging: submit on Devpost by 9am Sunday. Tables are assigned after the deadline; be at your table by 10:30am and stay until 12:30pm. Judges look at impact, quality, technical complexity and creativity. Prepare a two minute pitch with a live demo. Projects must be started during the event.
Slack: announcements, mentorship and team formation. Ask directors in #0-ask-directors, mentors in #1-ask-mentors. Never @channel. Join with the email you applied with.
Hackathons @ Berkeley app: holds your digital Hacker Pass, event bookmarks and venue maps. Sign in with your Hive email. Tap the profile icon then check for updates after installing.
Hardware: the Cal Hacks hardware rental booth, MLH hardware lab and 3D printing station are at the Hardware Desk on the mezzanine.
Workshop by Anthropic: Intro to Claude Code, boost your coding workflow. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Workshop by Meta: From chatbots to agent teams, agentic engineering at Meta. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Capital One hosts a Nintendo Smash Bros tournament on Saturday.
Workshop by Factory: Shipping with the Factory Droid SDK. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Workshop by Fetch.ai: Build, deploy and monetise AI agents with Fetch.ai, uAgents and Agentverse. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Workshop by Creao AI: From chat to backend, build an AI agent you can call from code. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Workshop by Hyphenate: Beyond agentic harnesses, engineering the autonomous enterprise. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Workshop by Bitdeer AI: Supercharging your hackathon project with Bitdeer Model Studio. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Workshop by Figma: From canvas to shipped, how to differentiate in the age of AI. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Workshop by Moss: Retrieval in 6 to 7 milliseconds with Moss, semantic search without a vector database. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Workshop by SpaceXAI: Build your entire internship application stack in 30 minutes. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Workshop by Convex: Build your backend with Convex. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Workshop by Microsoft: System design for deployed agents. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Workshop by Apify: Apify is your superpower for hackathons, web scraping and automation. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Workshop by Elastic: Build an agent that does the research, context engineering with Elasticsearch. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Fireside chat by Visa: AI and security in digital payments. Saturday in the Theater.
Technical domain talk by Annapurna Labs (Amazon chips). Saturday in the Theater.
Workshop by SpacetimeDB, details to be announced. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Workshop by Bright Data, details to be announced. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.
Workshop by AfterQuery, details to be announced. Saturday in the Workshop Rooms.

Cal Hacks general prizes: First Overall wins a MacBook Air 13 inch M5, Second Overall a Nintendo Switch 2, Third Overall Google intelligent eyewear. Most Creative Hack: Instax camera. Most Technically Complex: NuPhy Air60 HE keyboard. Best People-First Hack: Apple Watch SE 3. Best Planet-First Hack: America the Beautiful parks pass. Best Hardware Hack: Bambu Lab A1 Mini 3D printer. Best Beginner Hack: AirPods 4. Best Solo Hack: AirPods Pro 3. Hacker's Choice: Logitech MX Master 4.
Best Use of Moss sponsor track. Moss wants voice AI agents that listen and act in real time, personal agents that remember you across apps, or the best social post. Prize: AirPods Max or AirPods Pro.
Anthropic track: best use of Claude. Anthropic also runs the Intro to Claude Code workshop.

Best Use of Cartesia: build a useful voice experience where voice is core to the product. Submit a working demo, a two minute demo-first presentation and a short README. Judged 25% each on problem and originality, use of Cartesia, execution, impact and responsibility. Prize: Meta glasses.
Best Use of Fetch.ai: agents built with uAgents and Agentverse, reachable from ASI:One. Prizes: first $1500, second $1000, third $500.
SpacetimeDB track: real-time shared state, multiplayer interaction, live dashboards, AI agent coordination. SpacetimeDB must be meaningfully used. Prizes: first $2048, second $1024, third $512.
Best Use of Convex: backend with workflow, sync, search and file storage in TypeScript. Prize: $5000 cash.
Best Use of the Factory Droid SDK: Droid must do real work in the running product on a trigger you designed, with safety and visible plans and diffs. Prize: $2000 cash, credits and swag.
Best Use of Nessie by Capital One, judged on completeness, creativity and complexity. Prize: $300 Giftogram per person.

Meta track: Bringing people closer together with AI. Judged on strengthening human connection, how essential the AI is, originality and the demo. Prize: invitation to the Round 2 hackathon at Meta Menlo Park with travel covered, plus swag.
Best Use of x402 by Coinbase, two tracks. Prize: $500 USDC plus a recruiter call per team member per track, up to $4000 total.
Creao AI tracks: Best AI-First Disruptor, Best One-Person Company, Best Team Empowerment. $5000 total cash plus a year of CREAO Pro Max and Launchpad mentorship.

CRS Financial Intelligence Challenge: build on the CRS credit API sandbox and show it live. Best Overall CRS Hack $1000, Best Financial AI Agent $500, identity and fraud innovation and most unexpected use get interviews. Sandbox at calhacks.crscreditapi.com, find them at the CRS booth.

The Hyphenated Enterprise by Hyphenate: autonomous systems for finance, judged on realism, whether you would hire it, novelty and a defining moment. Cash prizes $8000, $5000, $3000 and expedited interviews for the top five teams.
Best Use of Notability: notes that show how the idea evolved using handwriting, audio, diagrams, PDFs and Smart Notes. Prize: one year of Notability Pro and merch.
Best Use of Bitdeer AI Model Studio: an AI application built on Model Studio. First place $500 credits and four gaming mice, second $200 credits and a LEGO Technic set.
Make it Legendary with SpaceXAI: a project built with Cursor using the Grok Imagine or Voice API on real space data. Prize: custom Cursor mechanical keyboard.
Best Use of Apify: web scraping and automation. Prizes from $1000 down to $400 for the top five.
Best Use of Reimagining Visa: judged on innovation, user experience, technical execution, commerce impact, trust and responsibility. Prize: $5000.
Best Security Hack sponsored by Armadin. Prize: Apple headphones, possibly hacking tools.
Figma track, details to be announced. Prize: Amazon gift cards and a session with the Figma early career recruiting team.
